# Number allocation

The four allocation registries, kept in one document because each is read AS A
TABLE: `CI-06f`, `CI-06h` and `CI-06p` call one shared parser over the first cell of
every row. A table split into a file per row is not a table, which is the same reason
`DELTA_MANIFEST` stays single under [ADR-043](ADR-043.md).

**Every table here carries two columns and no third.** The number, and who took it.
The State column that used to sit beside them is deleted, on [ADR-034](ADR-034.md)'s
own remedy, and the ruling is [below](#the-state-column-is-deleted-on-adr-034s-own-remedy).

## Number allocation, and why this table exists

**An ADR number is claimed here before it is written.** Two branches forking from the same `main` both read the registry, both find the same maximum, and both take the next integer. Neither is wrong locally; the corpus is broken the moment the second merges. **[ADR-034](ADR-034.md) rules the allocation, and [CI-06f](../testing/STRATEGY.md) enforces it.**

It is the two-ref gap this file documents at length, met a third time.

**Gaplessness is asserted over allocated plus reserved**, so a branch holding a reserved number shows a hole in this file and passes. A branch inventing an unreserved number fails.

**`053`, `054` and `055` were assigned to three parallel sessions within an hour of each other and none of them was reserved here at the time, so gaplessness was broken at every intermediate state and the first of the three to reach a commit paid for all of it.** The session holding `055` found `CI-06f` reporting `053` and `054` as holes, could not invent their subjects, and had to stop and ask. **That is a defect in how numbers are handed out, not in the gate**: `CI-06f` did exactly what [ADR-034](ADR-034.md) built it to do, which is refuse a sequence nobody can account for. The remedy is the one the `044` row below already names, applied at assignment time rather than at commit time: **a number is reserved in this table when it is handed out, by whoever hands it out, before the session that received it writes a line of anything.**

### `044` collided with an open sibling pull request, and this branch moved

**This session claimed `044`, wrote the ADR, the migration that cites it, its probe and eleven documents, and then found `044` already claimed by PR #25.** `main` ends at `043`, this branch is not behind `main`, and **twelve of twelve gates passed against that claim**, because `CI-06f` reads one ref and PR #25's branch is not it. **That is `CI-06f`'s declared coverage gap met in the wild for the second time in three days**, after [FOLD-02](../plans/FOLD-02-enforcement-window-and-suspension.md)'s plan hit it on `038`, and the cross-ref job that would close it is still not written.

**The remedy was a manual step this session skipped and the FOLD-02 session did not.** That session's record says "every remote branch was checked"; this one checked `main`, found `043`, and took `044`. **The table cannot do that step for you**: it is single-ref by construction, it says so in its own words two paragraphs down, and a claim made without reading the siblings is a claim made against a table that was never asked the question.

**It is resolved here rather than at merge**, which is FOLD-02's precedent rather than PR #4 and PR #5's: the founder assigned at merge once, [ADR-034](ADR-034.md) exists because that was expensive, and the branch that discovers a collision is the only one that can act on it. **This branch moved even though [ADR-034](ADR-034.md)'s tiebreak points the other way**, and the reasoning is worth the two lines it costs: the tiebreak renumbers the branch whose number is cited least, and this branch cites it forty-one times against PR #25's twenty-one, **including inside a migration**. But the tiebreak decides which branch _should_ move, and only one branch _can_. **PR #25 is open, complete and waiting for a founder who would otherwise resolve a numbering conflict in a frozen registry by hand**; this session was still writing. The number cited inside a migration is the one that matters, and `0033` is unmerged, so the citation is a `sed` rather than a supersession.

### The State column is deleted, on ADR-034's own remedy

**A third column used to sit beside these two and say `allocated` or `reserved, unmerged`. It was wrong eleven times in nine days**, and the rows recorded it against themselves, one repair at a time: `035` four commits after PR #9 merged it, `036` after PR #13, `037` and `038` after PR #15, `039` through `043` after PR #17 and PR #18, and `045` with the migration table's `0033` after PR #29. **[ADR-036](ADR-036.md) already ruled the column prose no gate can check**, [STRATEGY](../testing/STRATEGY.md) already declared it as a coverage gap, and the column went on rotting anyway, because a declared gap is a description of a defect rather than a fix for one.

**[ADR-034](ADR-034.md)'s remedy has exactly two branches: generate the value, or delete it and point at the source.** There is no third, and in particular hand-repairing the column is not one, because that is what was being done, eleven times. This file already applied the remedy once, to the next-free-number sentence in the migration section below. Applied to the column, it splits the old cell in two:

| What the cell claimed                                                                                                           | Disposition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Is the artifact in this tree?** `docs/decisions/ADR-045.md` exists here, `0035_rule_states_calendar_revision.sql` exists here | **DERIVED, at check time, from the tree.** `CI-06f` and `CI-06h` already compute exactly this set to assert gaplessness against these tables; `node scripts/corpus/gates.mjs allocation` prints it per row. A derivation that runs is worth more than a cell that agreed with the tree on the day somebody typed it                      |
| **Has the branch that claimed it merged?** `allocated` against `reserved, unmerged`                                             | **DELETED.** A runner reading one ref cannot tell a reservation from an allocation: the branch holding a reservation and the `main` that has absorbed it both show the number claimed. It is the two-ref problem [ADR-036](ADR-036.md) records, it is not closed here, and a claim no reader and no runner can check is not written down |

**Why the Claimed by column stays while the State column goes, which is the whole distinction.** A claimant is a historical fact and merging cannot falsify it: `merged to main (PR #17)` is true today and true forever, and a branch name records who to ask. **`reserved, unmerged` is false the instant the pull request merges, and nothing in the tree tells the row to change.** The volatile column is the one that was deleted, and it is the only one that ever drifted.

**What a reader loses, stated rather than glossed.** The table no longer says which claims are live. That was never a fact it held: it held a fact somebody entered, and the eleven instances are the measurement of how long that fact survived. What answers the question now is `git ls-remote`, which is the manual step the `044` collision above exists to teach, and `node scripts/corpus/gates.mjs allocation`, which answers the half a single ref can honestly answer.

**The duplicate rows are [`OI-11`](../STATE.md) and are not touched here.** Several numbers appear twice, a branch row beside the row recording that branch's merge, and choosing which of each pair survives is a decision rather than an edit. With the volatile column gone the pairs now differ only in their claimant, which is the form a dedup session will collapse.

## Migration number allocation, and why there is more than one table

**A migration number is claimed here before the file is written.** It is the same race as the one above, on the registry where it is least recoverable. **This heading read "why there are two tables" until a third arrived below it**, which is a hand-maintained count in the file that rules against them, one week old. [ADR-034](ADR-034.md) resolved the ADR collision by **renumbering the branch whose number was cited least**, and that remedy does not exist here: a migration is sacred once merged (constitution E2), so a number that has landed cannot be renamed, only superseded. **[ADR-036](ADR-036.md) rules the allocation and [CI-06h](../testing/STRATEGY.md) enforces it**, by the same rule as `CI-06f` and against this table.

They were not, and the sentence claiming nothing was reserved was **the only thing in the repository asserting it**, in the table that exists to end assertions of that kind. [ADR-034](ADR-034.md)'s remedy applies to it exactly: either generate the number or delete it and point at the source. **Deleted.** A session that needs a number adds its row here, and the row is what a sibling branch reads. **That deletion is the precedent the State column was repaired on**, one section up and one week later.

**And it is claimed BEFORE the file is written, in its own commit, which this sentence used to say the opposite of.** It read "in the same commit that creates the file", and that is a claim a sibling branch cannot see until the work is done: the whole window this table exists to close is the one between deciding on a number and having something to show for it, which is exactly the window a same-commit claim leaves open. [ADR-034](ADR-034.md) already rules the order for an ADR number ("claimed here before it is written") and the sentence over the registry where a collision is **unrecoverable** was the looser of the two. **The founder ruled the stricter reading on 2026-08-16** and `0033`'s row above is the first claim made under it: committed and pushed on its own, then the file.

**The same two-ref limit applies.** This table makes a collision visible to the second branch **that reads `main`**; it cannot stop a branch that never looks. The cross-branch assertion, that a pull request may not claim a number already on `main`, needs a job that can see both refs and belongs with `CI-06f`'s identical gap.

### `0034` was claimed twice IN THIS TABLE, and twelve gates read it and passed

**Two rows above both claim `0034`.** [ADR-047](ADR-047.md) claimed it for `rule_states`' calendar revision; `ADR-046` claimed it for the reversible contact addresses, wrote the file, and merged in PR #41. **The number is spent, so this migration is `0035`** and the row above records the move.

**This one was not the two-ref gap.** The ADR-044 collision two headings up was invisible because `CI-06f` reads one ref and the colliding claim lived on another. **This collision was in one file, on one ref, in adjacent rows, and every gate still passed** — because `allocated()` in [`gates.mjs`](../../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs) accumulates claims into a `Set`. Two rows claiming `0034` produce one member. Gaplessness holds, "every number on disk is claimed" holds, and **a table whose entire purpose is to make a duplicate claim visible cannot see one.**

**That is worth more than the collision it let through**, because the ADR remedy does not exist on this registry: [ADR-034](ADR-034.md) renumbers the branch citing the number least, and a merged migration cannot be renumbered at all (constitution E2). **Here the recovery was free only because the second file was still unwritten.**

The check is a handful of lines against a `Set` that already exists, and it is **not written in this session, for a stated reason**: the tables are full of duplicate rows today. The ADR table above claims `039` through `046` **twice each**, a branch row beside the row recording that branch's merge, and this table claims `0033` twice as well as `0034`. So the assertion fails on arrival and what it needs first is a cleanup of the historical record, which is a session and a decision about which of each pair survives rather than a gate. It is [`OI-11`](../STATE.md), raised by the branch that met it, and it is the same shape as `OI-10`: **a duplicate that a gate reading for presence cannot see.**

## CI gate identifier allocation, and why there are now three tables

**THIS TABLE IS CLOSED. It allocates nothing and it is now a DECODER**, per [ADR-131](ADR-131.md). The `CI-06<letter>` series ends at **`w`**, `x`, `y` and `z` are **retired unused**, and every gate written from here takes a slug, `CI-06/<subject>`, per [ADR-065](ADR-065.md) section 5. **The twenty three letters below keep their names**, because 2,563 citations across 283 files resolve against them and 145 of those files are dated session records that [ADR-118](ADR-118.md) rules may not be rewritten. **`CI-06/closed-letter-series` enforces the closure**: a row added below is a finding, in this runner, on every pull request.

([ADR-085](ADR-085.md) section 4.)

**ONE SPECIFIED GATE HOLDS NO LETTER, AND THAT IS [ADR-065](ADR-065.md) SECTION 4 RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.** [ADR-059](ADR-059.md)'s **M01-column gate** -- every column M01 declares is reachable from an engine input -- was reserved as `CI-06u` by [session 75](../sessions/2026-08-19-session-75.md) while a different `CI-06u` was already shipping. The shipped gate keeps the letter. **The displaced one is deliberately NOT given the next free letter**: section 5 of that ADR measures that there is none. `a` through `w` are claimed, [`nextFreeLetter()`](../../scripts/corpus/falsify.mjs) scans `a` to `x` only, and the `CI-06p` seed consumes the free letter plus two above it, so `x`, `y` and `z` are the harness's headroom and not an allocation. **No row may claim `x`.** The gate is specified in ADR-059 and is **permanently unlettered**: [ADR-131](ADR-131.md) closes the series rather than migrating it, so when that gate is written it takes a slug like every other gate written since ADR-065.

**One letter in this file is already spoken for by something that is not a gate, and it is named here so a reader does not mistake it for a reservation.** [ADR-036](ADR-036.md)'s alternatives list rejects "**`CI-06k`, a sibling of `CI-06f`**" by name. That `CI-06k` was never written and never claimed; the letter is FOLD-01's. **This is the failure mode the shared allocation parser was hardened against on the other two tables**, where a three-digit numeral in prose used to reserve a number silently, and it is why the first cell of a table row is the only thing that claims anything here either.

**This table is read by `CI-06p` now, which is the remedy this section named for itself and then went a week without.** It said "the cheap version of the gate is the one to write: uniqueness of the letters in the STRATEGY rows, and gaplessness over allocated plus reserved, which is `CI-06f`'s assertion with a different alphabet". That is what `CI-06p` is, and it reads letters through a parser of its own rather than through `allocated()`, because `allocated()` parses a three-digit or four-digit first cell and **a letter does not parse**, which is why nothing read this table for a week while two gates read the tables above it.

**Its third assertion is the one that keeps the table from going vacuous, and it is `CI-06h`'s.** Gaplessness alone cannot force a row: a letter implemented in the runner already fills its own hole, so the sequence stays gapless while the registry stops being maintained. **Every letter the runner holds must therefore be claimed by a row here**, exactly as every migration number on disk must be claimed by a row above.

### `ADR-046` was allocated twice IN ONE FILE, and the gate that checks for it could not run

**`docs/decisions/ADR-046.md` carried two `## ADR-046` headings** for two unrelated rulings: `OQ-P2-01`'s `CalendarSlice` ruling and `OQ-M10-06`'s reversible contact addresses. It was created by merging PR #40 and PR #41, neither of which had checked that the other claimed the number.

**This was not the two-ref gap and it was not a missing assertion either.** `CI-06f` has carried `if (seen.has(n)) findings.push("ADR-nnn appears more than once")` since it was written. **It could never fire**: `adrEntries()` in [`gates.mjs`](../../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs) read each file with a **non-global** `exec`, returning at most one entry per file, so two headings produced one entry and `seen` never collided. Fifteen gates passed over the duplicate.

**`ADR-049` is the one that moved, on a count rather than a guess**: 25 citing lines in 6 files against 70 in 20. And decisively, **37 of the other ruling's citations sit inside [`0034`](../../packages/db/migrations/0034_reversible_contact_addresses.sql), a merged migration constitution E2 forbids editing**, so that ruling was not renumberable at all. [ADR-034](ADR-034.md)'s tiebreak and E2 agree here, which they will not always do: **on this registry the ADR remedy and the migration rule can point in opposite directions**, and when they do, E2 wins because it is the one that cannot be complied with retroactively.

**The parser was tightened only after a seed was watched not firing.** `CI-06f/duplicate-heading` in [`falsify.mjs`](../../scripts/corpus/falsify.mjs) reported `DID NOT FAIL` against the non-global parser and `in scope, failed` after it, in that order, because tightening a parser without one is how 109 phantom anchors happened.

## `OI-nn` allocation, and why the fourth table is here rather than in the manifest

**An `OI` number is claimed HERE, in the commit that opens the item.** [ADR-074](ADR-074.md)
section 7 ruled it: `OI`'s allocation moves to this file as a fourth table, **superseding
[`DELTA_MANIFEST` section 16](../../packages/db/DELTA_MANIFEST.md)**, whose `OI-nn` half now
records the items that manifest opened and allocates nothing.

**The premise that put the table in `packages/db/` has expired**, in the manifest's own words.
Section 16 was written under [ADR-034](ADR-034.md) after two collisions in one day, on the
stated argument that _"`OI-nn` and the section numbers are this document's own namespace"_.
`OI-16` onward were opened by sessions about gate coverage, lint scope, the letter registry
and the fixture inventory. **None of that is a schema-delta manifest's namespace**, and the
manifest's table shows it: it holds nineteen numbers over twenty rows and stops at `OI-24`.

**That gap is not theoretical and it is why this table exists.** [Session 120](../sessions/2026-08-21-session-120.md)
read section 16, found `OI-24` as the maximum, and took `OI-25` -- which
[WAVE-04 section 6](../plans/WAVE-04-fixture-backlog-and-gate-inventory.md) and
[STATE](../STATE.md) had already allocated. It was renumbered to `OI-27` and the near-miss
was recorded as `OI-27` itself. **The same shape had already happened twice more and nothing
had counted them**, which the three multiply-claimed rows below now state:

**Three numbers are claimed twice and none is renumbered here**, on the manifest's own
standing ruling: _"two rows sharing an identifier is a defect; two rows sharing an identifier
with no way to say which one you mean is a worse one, and it costs three words to close."_
Every one of the six rows carries its subject in the first cell, which is what makes them six
distinct keys to `CI-06u` and what lets a citation say which item it means. **Renumbering any
of them breaks every citation of whichever one moves**, and on `OI-19` and `OI-20` the
renumber has already happened once, in WAVE-04, without STATE being able to follow it.

**What a gate could read, named and not written.** [`CI-06w`](../testing/STRATEGY.md) already
reads the three tables above as multisets, one key to at most one row; **extending it to this
table is the check that would have caught session 120**, because WAVE-04's claim and session
120's would have been two rows over one key in one file. It is a fourth entry in a list the
runner already walks, and it is not written here because
[`scripts/corpus/`](../../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs) is outside this session's fence.

**`CI-06/identifier-series` does NOT promote `OI` on this commit, and that is measured rather
than assumed.** [ADR-074](ADR-074.md) section 7 predicts _"the day that table lands this entry
stops naming a defect and the gate fails until `OI` is promoted in the same commit"_. **It does
not fail**, because the pending assertion fires only when EVERY member of a pending series has
exactly one definition site, and no reading of this tree comes close. **Counted on the commit
before this one: seven of the twenty-nine members had exactly one, fifteen had two or more,
and seven (`OI-17` to `OI-23`) had NONE**, since STATE defines those with a bold lead and
ADR-074 rules that a bold lead is not a definition site. **Counted after it: six of thirty
have exactly one and twenty-four have two or more**, because this table adds a site to every
member it names. **Reconciling all thirty to one site each is the promotion, and it is a
session rather than a table**; this table is the allocator that session will promote `OI`
onto. The gate was run in both states rather than reasoned about: 28 of 28 before and after.

## `RI-nn` allocation, and why the fifth table is here

**A repository invariant number is claimed in PROSE, inside an ADR body, where a grep for the next
free number does not look.** `RI-08` was named in [ADR-096](ADR-096.md) section 9 and assigned to
`P4-e`; `P4-e` landed without it and the number sat claimed and unwritten for eight days while
[ADR-095](ADR-095.md) `F4` and its section 9 item 5b cited the same hole. `RI-10` was taken the same
way. **That is `OI-27`'s class exactly**, and it is the class the four tables above exist to end for
ADR numbers, migration numbers, `CI-06` letters and `OI` items.

**THIS TABLE IS AN ALLOCATOR AND IT IS NOT THE `RI` SERIES REPAIR.**
[`gates.mjs`](../../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs)'s `PENDING_SERIES` holds `RI` with the reason _"a table
in the tooling README; members have no row"_, and [`packages/tooling/README.md`](../../packages/tooling/README.md)'s
table does stop at `RI-05`. **That README is outside session 229's fence and is unedited**, so the
pending entry stands and [ADR-117](ADR-117.md) section 7 rows it. Two tables for one identifier is
this corpus's ordinary shape rather than a defect: every ADR has a row here and a row in
[`decisions/README.md`](README.md) under `CI-06n`. **The claim is stated so nobody later reads the
allocator as the repair.**

**THE ROWS ARE READ OUT OF [`repo-invariants.mjs`](../../packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs)'s
`CHECKS` ARRAY, NEVER TYPED.** `RI-04`'s and `RI-09`'s titles are COMPUTED from `DEPLOYABLES` in that
file, so a sixth deployable moves this table's text without an edit here. A second copy of those
titles would drift the day the list grew, which is `RI-04`'s own header: _"Two lists is the defect;
one list read twice is the fix."_

**`CI-06/identifier-series` WAS PROBED IN BOTH SHAPES BEFORE THIS TABLE WAS WRITTEN.** That gate fails
a `PENDING_SERIES` entry whose every member has exactly one definition site, demanding a promotion in
`gates.mjs`, which is another session's fence. A ten-row probe and a five-row probe (the members with
no README row) were each appended here and the gate run against each: **both reported 30 of 30**, and
both probes were removed with `git status --porcelain` clean after.
